title: Eval & Quality Monitoring Demo — Verdant Health
summary: Redwood demo focused on Eval & Quality Monitoring: how prompt sets are organized, creating regression alerts tied to test prompts, and running A/B comparisons between model variants using Redwood Console and API. Customer (Verdant Health) is evaluating for clinical summarization pipeline; primary concerns were privacy (PHI), reproducible evals, and clear alerting thresholds. AE Jordan + SE Priya walked through Console dashboards, Optimize suggestions, and a short API demo with prompt set import. Action items and follow-ups agreed (send security docs, SOC2, sample prompt set template, and schedule pilot benchmarks).
action_items: Jordan Ellis — Send SOC2 + security pack and SOC2 attestation link — 2025-09-29
Priya Nambiar — Share sample prompt-set CSV and evaluation templates, plus demo recording — 2025-09-26
Dr. Aaron Liu — Provide 3 canonical prompt examples and target success criteria (precision/recall or ROUGE) — 2025-10-03
Miguel Santos — Confirm legal/data residency requirements and internal timeline for POC — 2025-10-01
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2 report
Customer to share representative prompt set and success metrics
Schedule 2-hour POC kickoff to run benchmarks (model A/B) — propose next week
Priya to set up temporary test project and invite Verdant engineers
questions: Can Redwood run A/B comparisons across quantized model variants with preserved KV cache behavior?
How are regression alerts configured and can they be tied to specific prompt sets/labels?
What telemetry is available for token-level latencies and cost breakdowns per route?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Ellis, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya Nambiar, our SE. Quick intros?
[00:12] Sarah (Verdant): Sarah Kim, Head of ML at Verdant Health.
[00:15] Aaron: Aaron Liu, clinical data team.
[00:18] Miguel: Miguel Santos, VP Engineering.
[00:22] Jordan: Great. The plan today is a focused demo on Eval and Quality Monitoring — prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. We'll show Console and a quick API flow, and then leave time for Q&A. Sound good?
[00:32] Sarah: Yep, that's exactly what we need — especially the alerting piece; we can't have silent regressions in clinical summaries.
[00:38] Priya (Redwood): Perfect. I'll start by sharing my screen — opening the Redwood Console. (screen share) You should see the Eval tab, and a project called "verdant-pilot" that has some example prompt sets.
[00:52] [00:55] Priya: So on the left here are prompt sets — you can group prompts by use case like "discharge-summary" or "medication-extraction". Each prompt has metadata: tags, expected labels, and golden answers. We support CSV imports or direct API ingestion.
[01:10] Aaron: Quick question — when you say "golden answers", does Redwood store PHI? How is that protected?
[01:17] Jordan: Good callout. We have options: you can store golden data encrypted at rest with your KMS, or keep them in your VPC/private deployment. We'll send the security deck with details.
[01:27] Sarah: Also curious about retention — we need logs for audits for 7 years in some cohorts.
[01:33] Priya: We can configure retention and export audit logs; plus we integrate with SIEM via the audit API. We'll include the endpoints in the pack.
[01:42] [02:00] Priya: Back to demo — here's the Eval dashboard. You get aggregate metrics (accuracy, exact match, ROUGE) per prompt set, and you can break down by model variant or by date.
[02:15] Priya: Now, regression alerts — you define a baseline window and a threshold, e.g., a 5% drop in exact match over the last 1,000 prompts triggers an alert. Alerts can route to Slack, PagerDuty, or trigger an automated rollback.
[02:31] Miguel: Can alerts be scoped to weighted prompts? We have high-risk prompts for critical summaries.
[02:36] Priya: Yes, you can tag prompts as "critical" and set stricter thresholds. Also you can create grouped alerts that only fire if multiple metrics degrade.
[02:47] [03:10] Sarah: How do A/B comparisons work? We need to test model updates and quantized variants side-by-side.
[03:18] Priya: Great question. We have an A/B runner in Optimize — you can route a percentage of traffic to model A vs B, collect eval metrics on the shared prompt set, and view per-prompt diffs. It preserves KV cache semantics between variants if they're compatible; if not compatible we'll surface the differences in latency and hit rates.
[03:40] Aaron: Compatibility meaning different quantization or sequence-length behavior?
[03:44] Priya: Exactly. If you compare a 4-bit quantized variant to a full float checkpoint, caching and latency can differ. Redwood marks variants as "fallback-safe" or not.
[03:55] [04:10] Jordan: We also have API examples — you can push prompts via the Eval API endpoint, get back structured results including token-level alignments and the model output. For example: POST /v1/eval/promptset with a CSV.
[04:26] Miguel: Is there rate limiting for eval ingestion? We'll be streaming a few million prompts during POC.
[04:33] Priya: We support bulk uploads and streaming. For large ingests we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment for predictable throughput. We can proposal reserved capacity for the POC.
[04:43] [05:00] Sarah: For our use case, we need reproducible evals for regulatory audit — can we pin seeds and model versions?
[05:07] Priya: Yes, you can pin model versions, quantization profile, and PRNG seeds for sampling-based metrics. The Console also exports a reproducible run manifest you can store alongside results.
[05:18] Aaron: When you export results, do you export the prompts and outputs as well?
[05:22] Priya: You can choose full export (prompts + outputs + metadata) or strip PII before export. Also we have integration with customer KMS for encryption on export.
[05:34] [06:00] [slight crosstalk] Sarah: I'm seeing in the demo a chart called "Regression heatmap" — what drives the heatmap?
[06:08] Priya: The heatmap is per-prompt-type vs metric delta. It highlights clusters where many prompts degrade. You can click a cell to drill into the prompt examples that drove the signal.
[06:20] Jordan: We often pair that with a canary rollout: if the heatmap shows a problem, Redwood can auto-fallback the route to the prior stable model.
[06:30] Miguel: Nice. For our internal processes, we'd like an automated ticket created when a regression hits a critical tag.
[06:36] Priya: You can connect to Jira; we have webhook templates that create a ticket with the top failing prompts and suggested rollback action.
[06:45] [07:15] Aaron: About A/B, do you store per-variant token-level costs so we can compare economics?
[07:22] Priya: Yes — Console shows token-level cost, latency percentiles, and effective cost-per-correct-answer for each variant. That's part of Optimize recommendations: it suggests quantization profiles or batching tweaks to meet cost targets while maintaining QA thresholds.
[07:38] Sarah: Are those recommendations automated or human-reviewed?
[07:42] Jordan: They are suggestions; you can auto-apply policies if you trust them or keep them as manual quick wins. For regulated workloads we usually recommend a manual review before applying changes.
[07:52] [08:30] Priya: Quick demo of creating a regression alert: click "New Alert", choose prompt set, metric (exact_match), baseline window, and threshold. You can add a suppression window for known noisy times.
[08:46] Priya: I'll create a sample alert for the "discharge-summary" set at 4% drop. Save. Now you can preview the simulated triggers based on historical data.
[09:00] Sarah: That preview is helpful. Can we tune sensitivity per prompt?
[09:05] Priya: Yes, you can set per-prompt overrides or priority weights.
[09:12] [09:45] Miguel: Let's talk integration. We use Kubeflow and have most inference routed through our internal gateway. How does Redwood fit?
[09:53] Jordan: For hosted customers we offer a simple API; for hybrid you can deploy Redwood Private in your VPC and point your gateway at it. We also provide a small sidecar for easier telemetry.
[10:05] Sarah: Any compatibility issues with our K8s versions?
[10:08] Priya: We support modern K8s >= 1.22 for the on-prem package; for older clusters we can discuss a managed VPC option.
[10:15] [10:40] Aaron: For our clinical summaries we have golden labels with PHI redaction. Does Redwood do automated redaction in evals?
[10:48] Priya: We provide PII detection plugins and a redaction pipeline you can run before storing golden answers. Alternatively keep goldens behind your KMS.
[10:58] Sarah: How do we test edge-case prompts? We want monthly regression reports and highlight edge cases.
[11:05] Priya: Use weighted prompt sets and label prompts as "edge-case"; schedule recurring eval runs and exports. The reporting engine can produce monthly PDFs and CSVs.
[11:18] [11:50] Jordan: Quick API snippet: you can call /v1/ab-run with traffic split, attach prompt set id, and Redwood will collect metrics for the chosen duration. Post-run we produce a diff report and a per-prompt signed URL to the examples.
[12:06] Miguel: Is the signed URL ephemeral?
[12:08] Priya: Yes, configurable TTL.
[12:12] [12:40] Sarah: We heard mention of KV cache earlier — our models are chat-based and rely heavily on cache. If we A/B different model architectures, how do you handle cache replays?
[12:50] Priya: We replay prefixes where possible and translate cache keys when compatible. If architectures differ, we flag higher variance in early tokens and show that in the report. Sometimes mis-transcriptions here, it shows "K V cache" in the export but that's the same KV cache.
[13:05] Aaron: Good, we need that visibility.
[13:10] [13:30] Jordan: Wanted to surface Optimize's suggestion engine — it looks at your workload distribution, sequence lengths, and latency SLOs and recommends batching thresholds and quant profiles.
[13:42] Priya: I'll open a sample Optimize report — here it recommends switching to a 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical prompts and keeping full precision for critical ones. It also suggests a 64-token batching window to reduce cost by ~18%.
[13:58] Sarah: Sounds promising. How aggressive are these quantization suggestions on clinical text? We can't sacrifice extractive accuracy.
[14:06] Priya: The suggestion is risk-aware — it runs offline evals on your prompt set and simulates quality impact. It shows per-metric deltas so you can decide.
[14:18] [14:50] Miguel: For the POC we'd like to run an A/B between our current model and Redwood-curated open model with quantized variant. Can you run that inside the POC?
[14:59] Jordan: Absolutely — typical POC: we ingest prompt set, run A/B for X days, produce diff report, and then propose changes. We'll need your prompt set and success metrics.
[15:10] Sarah: On success metrics: we want both automatic metrics (ROUGE, exact match) and human-in-the-loop labels for high-risk prompts. Can Redwood incorporate human labels into evals?
[15:19] Priya: Yes — we have a Human Eval integration; results feed back into the eval dataset and update metrics. You can also gate rollouts on a human-approved pass rate.
[15:33] Aaron: Any concerns about model hallucinations specific to clinical context?
[15:37] Jordan: Hallucinations are a big focus — our eval harness includes fact-checking plugins and domain-specific checks. For clinical pipelines, we usually recommend conservative defaults and stronger human review windows.
[15:49] [16:10] Sarah: On compliance: will you send SOC2, ISO, and data flow diagrams?
[16:16] Jordan: Yes — we'll attach the security pack. Priya: we'll include a short architecture diagram for the Private deployment in VPC.
[16:24] Miguel: Regarding pricing for POC — do you have a flat POC price or usage-based?
[16:29] Jordan: We offer a POC package — modest committed usage for the POC timeframe with discounted rates. For heavy ingest we recommend a short reserved capacity to ensure throughput.
[16:40] [17:05] Priya: I'll show the per-prompt drilldown; click on a failing prompt, you get model outputs, history, and suggested prompt rephrasing. There's also a built-in A/B diff view that color-codes tokens where outputs diverge.
[17:22] Sarah: That token diff view will be useful for triage.
[17:26] [17:50] Aaron: Is there built-in tooling for creating prompt variations and running them as part of the prompt set?
[17:57] Priya: Yes — you can generate prompt variations or upload suggested rephrases and run them as child prompts. The eval harness will show which phrasing performed better.
[18:10] Miguel: For the POC, we'll need an onboarding doc for our infra team.
[18:15] Jordan: We'll send a POC checklist and a runbook.
[18:20] [18:55] Sarah: Quick nit — in the UI I saw a "model catalogue" — are those Redwood curated models or can we add our own?
[19:03] Priya: Both. There's Redwood-curated open models and verified performance profiles; you can also add custom models and register them with a version and quant profile.
[19:15] Miguel: Any limitations on model size for Private deployment?
[19:18] Priya: We support a range — 7B up to multi-100B via sharded deployments; for the largest checkpoints we recommend Dedicated clusters.
[19:30] [20:00] Jordan: Let's cover the POC timeline: Day 0 ingest prompts, Day 1 run baseline, Days 2–5 A/B runs, Day 6 produce report and retrospective. Typical POC is 2 weeks to include human labeling.
[20:13] Sarah: That fits our timeline; we are hoping to decide by mid-October.
[20:18] Aaron: On legal/data residency — we must keep everything in us-east for certain datasets.
[20:25] Jordan: We can pin region and/or run Private in your VPC. We'll confirm in the security pack.
[20:32] [21:00] Priya: One more advanced note — you can write custom evaluation hooks (Python) and upload them; Redwood will execute them in a sandboxed runner and surface results. That's useful for domain-specific checks.
[21:15] Sarah: Good — we have clinical heuristics that we'd like to run as custom hooks.
[21:20] Priya: Perfect. We'll include docs and a sample hook in the repo.
[21:30] [22:00] Miguel: Will you also provide cost projections for scaling to production? We need a 6-month estimate.
[22:08] Jordan: We can run a cost model based on your prompt volume and sequence lengths — Priya will prepare that as part of the POC materials.
[22:18] [23:00] Sarah: Any final items — competition-wise, is there anything Redwood can't do compared to self-host?
[23:07] Jordan: Self-host gives total control but higher ops burden. Redwood focuses on runtime optimization and observability; some ultra-custom kernel work might require close partnership but we can support it.
[23:20] Aaron: Sounds reasonable.
[23:25] [24:00] Priya: I'll now show a brief API call to run a quick eval on a single prompt — (types) you get a JSON with output, aligned tokens, and metric suggestions.
[24:18] [24:45] [minor transcription glitch: "console lags"]
[25:05] Jordan: OK, recap: we'll send security pack and SOC2, sample prompt-set template and Evaluate CSV, propose POC dates, and set up a test project with temporary creds.
[25:20] Sarah: We'll send 3 canonical prompts and our success criteria.
[25:25] Miguel: Legal will follow up regarding residency and contract terms.
[25:30] Jordan: Perfect. Any last Qs?
[25:34] Aaron: One more — can Redwood surface which prompts cause hallucinations vs factual errors separately?
[25:41] Priya: Yes, our eval schemas differentiate hallucination-type checks vs factual regressions; you can tag and alert separately.
[25:50] Sarah: Great. Thanks — this was useful.
[25:55] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll get the docs over by Monday.
[26:01] [end of recording — remaining 19 minutes: Q&A and setup details, roughly captured in action items and next steps]
